analysis.investment_thesis: MethodHub ranks decently on ROC (~31%) but only modestly on earnings yield (EBIT 17 / EV ~183 = ~9.3%), below Greenblatt's 12% attractiveness threshold. The Magic Formula requires BOTH cheap and good — this is good but not cheap enough, especially given weak cash conversion.
key_strengths: ROCE 31% and ROE 42.7% indicate high return on capital employed
Revenue nearly 4x in 2 years (35→135 Cr) with EBIT margin ~13% maintained
OCF positive all 3 years; low CWIP implies capital-light IT services model
key_risks: OCF of just 5 Cr vs net profit 11 Cr — poor cash conversion, working-capital absorption
Finance cost 5 Cr on EBIT 17 Cr (29%) is high for an IT services firm; borrowings at 39 Cr
Low promoter holding at 26.85% and tiny 144 Cr microcap — execution/governance risk
red_flags: Net profit 11 Cr but OCF only 5 Cr — earnings quality gap
Equity jumped 11→57 Cr in 2025 (likely IPO dilution) inflating ROE optics
Unusually high debt for a services business with minimal fixed-asset needs
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Magic Formula arithmetic: EBIT of 17 Cr against an EV of roughly 183 Cr (MCap 144 + Debt 39) yields an earnings yield of ~9.3% — acceptable but not in the top decile I look for (>12%). ROC is the stronger leg here: with modest net fixed assets and working capital, EBIT/Capital comfortably clears 25%+, consistent with the reported 31% ROCE. So this is a "good business at a fair price" rather than a "good business at a bargain" — the Magic Formula prefers the latter.

The red flag for me is cash conversion: EBIT 17 Cr but OCF just 5 Cr means receivables/WIP are soaking up the reported profits, which is typical of fast-growing IT services chasing enterprise clients but undermines the earnings yield's reliability. Combined with 29% of EBIT eaten by finance costs and a recent equity infusion that has yet to be efficiently deployed, the systematic rank lands in the middle of the pack. I'd pass unless the price corrected meaningfully or next-year EBIT showed matching OCF.
